question: How can a developer advance ledgers quickly in Stellar Quickstart to test time-dependent contract behavior?

golden.answer: For current Quickstart local mode, ordinary --local auto-closes roughly every second through testing acceleration. To control closes, start with --enable-core-manual-close (default false), which sets Core MANUAL_CLOSE, then call manualclose; each current call advances one ledger. A requested count parameter remains open in stellar-core issue #4040. Repeated closes advance sequence and close time but do not set an arbitrary timestamp. Under Protocol 30 (CAP-88; the current Quickstart image default as of 2026-11-02), close time has millisecond resolution, so rapid closes can share one whole-second contract timestamp. Use soroban-sdk ledger test utilities for direct unit-test timestamp/sequence mutation, and Quickstart for Core/RPC/TTL/archive integration. Pin the image, and use a fresh volume or explicit reconfiguration if initialized supervisor/service configuration conflicts with changed flags.

golden.notes: Status-sensitive details are stated as of 2026-11-02; grade later sourced changes leniently and require dated primary evidence. Do not penalize an answer that sets ENABLE_CORE_MANUAL_CLOSE=true as a container environment variable: the current start script still reads it as the default for --enable-core-manual-close, although the docs show only the flag. Standalone Core with RUN_STANDALONE=true accepts ledgerSeq and closeTime parameters on manualclose (closeTime must still be later than the last close). Quickstart does not set RUN_STANDALONE, so an answer that scopes those parameters to standalone Core is correct; claiming them for Quickstart is not. From Protocol 30 (CAP-88), consecutive ledgers may share the same whole-second closeTime and Soroban ledger timestamp; a claim that every manualclose advances env.ledger().timestamp() by at least one second is wrong unless the answer scopes it to Protocol 29 or earlier.
